intro.headline: Can you still tell what's real?
intro.body: Generative AI makes fake faces, video, art and chat cheap and convincing — which is exactly what social engineers exploit. Test yourself against each tool below, then use the coach and personal path to turn what fooled you into a habit that won't.

sections.title: Test your media literacy
sections.instruction: Individual assignment. Evaluate your ability to detect AI-generated media — deepfakes, realistic faces, videos, artwork, and chat — by testing yourself across these online tools. For each: record how you did and note the cue that gave it away (or fooled you).

fields.instr: Try the deepfake detection test and see how many you can detect.
fields.answer: How many did you catch, and what gave the fakes away?

fields.instr: Try to detect real faces vs. AI-generated faces.
fields.answer: Which face details gave the AI ones away?
What in the video signalled AI?
What gave the AI art away?

fields.instr: See if you can detect if you're talking to a human or AI.
fields.answer: What in the conversation tipped you off?

debrief.prompt: Across the tools, what most reliably exposed AI media — and how would you verify a suspicious image, voice or message in real life?

rubric.name: Names a concrete cue
rubric.description: Identifies a specific detection signal (face/eye/hand artifacts, blink/lip-sync drift, garbled text or impossible geometry, evasive/memory-less chat).

rubric.name: States a verification habit
rubric.description: Gives the reliable habit: no single tool is proof — corroborate against a trusted source and confirm identity out of band before acting.

rubric.name: Links to social engineering
rubric.description: Connects synthetic media to how attackers weaponize it against people (deepfake voice/video, AI phishing).

rubric.name: Calibrated confidence
rubric.description: Recognizes detection is probabilistic; avoids over-trusting a single verdict or tool.

quality_rules: Coach never helps create deepfakes or deceptive media.
Coach never declares a specific item definitely real or fake; detection is probabilistic.
Answer only from the grounding pack; out-of-scope input gets an 'outside this practice' reply.
Feedback is 2-3 sentences, plain, no lists.
No student PII is sent; redact before any AI call.

outcome_logic.focus: AI faces fooled you. Next time scan eyes, teeth, ears, hair edges, jewelry and background for asymmetry or warping — but remember no single detail is proof.
AI video fooled you. Watch for unnatural blinking, lip-sync drift and lighting/edge artifacts — and for any instruction on video, confirm out of band before acting.
AI art fooled you. Look for garbled text, impossible geometry and too-perfect texture; treat provenance, not polish, as the signal.
The chatbot fooled you. Generic, evasive or memory-less answers are tells — and this is exactly the social-engineering surface, so never act on identity claimed in chat alone.
Topic 1 shows how AI both builds these lures and detects them. Carry the habit: unverified media is unverified until you corroborate it.
